newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA TO INTRODUCE EARLY RETIREMENT INCENTIVES.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA TO INTRODUCE EARLY RETIREMENT INCENTIVES.

text.p: The Venezuelan government announced Wednesday an early retirement incentive plan to ease the process of cutting its massive state payroll.

Under the decree approved by the cabinet, public sector workers taking voluntary retirement will receive an additional 50 percent on top of their usual severance pay, Information Minister Fernando Egana said.
"This decree is very important because it is a step forward to ease the process of restructuring the public administration," Egana told reporters at Miraflores presidential palace.
He said the bonus payments should help speed up the reduction of Venezuela's 1.3 million public sector workforce.
Egana gave no details of how many workers the government hoped to cut from its payroll, or how much the incentive plan would cost.
He said workers who resigned voluntarily would be incorporated into job creation and training schemes to ease their move into the private sector.
Reduction of its bloated state bureaucracy is seen by analysts as one of the main challenges facing the Venezuelan government in coming years.
